'''Tie:''' {{legend0|#ae8bb1|50%}} {{legend0|#808080|No data}} | turnout = 50.86% {{decrease}} }} {{ElectionsSC}} The '''2022 South Carolina gubernatorial election''' took place on November 8, 2022, to elect the [[governor of South Carolina]]. Incumbent [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] Governor [[Henry McMaster]] ran for re-election for a second full term in office and secured the Republican nomination in the June 14 primary. [[Joe Cunningham (American politician)|Joe Cunningham]], former [[United States representative]] from [[South Carolina's 1st congressional district]], was the Democratic nominee.{{cite web |title=South Carolina Primary Results |url=https://www.cnn.com/election/2022/results/south-carolina/primaries |website=CNNpolitics |publisher=CNN |access-date=15 June 2022}} McMaster won the general election with 58% of the vote — a 4.08% improvement over his [[2018 South Carolina gubernatorial election|2018]] margin. McMaster became the first Republican gubernatorial candidate to win [[Calhoun County, South Carolina|Calhoun County]] since [[1994 South Carolina gubernatorial election|1994]], and the first to win [[Clarendon County, South Carolina|Clarendon County]] and [[Dillon County, South Carolina|Dillon County]] since [[1990 South Carolina gubernatorial election|1990]]. This election marks the largest gubernatorial victory in the state since [[1990 South Carolina gubernatorial election|1990]], when incumbent Republican [[Carroll A.
